Wider Sports News.title: HSBC: 80 years of banking on the UAE’s ambition
Wider Sports News.summary: HSBC: 80 years of banking on the UAE’s ambition Gulf News
Wider Sports News.copy:
On October 12, 1946, an international bank opened a small branch beside Dubai Creek. It was the first bank ever in Dubai. It was the result of a meeting between Frank Johnson, a manager of the Imperial Bank, with the late Sheikh Saeed Bin Maktoum Al Maktoum and his son, the late Sheikh Rashid Bin Saeed Al Maktoum. Johnson found rulers who already saw Dubai as a place the world would come to trade.

Eighty years on, that bank is HSBC Bank Middle East and the town it served is one of the world’s great centres of trade and finance. The partnership in Dubai began with infrastructure. In 1954, the bank worked to help raise the loan for dredging the Creek, the project that opened the city to larger vessels and set the pattern for the port-led growth that followed. As the Emirates grew, so did our presence: Sharjah in 1953, Abu Dhabi in 1959, and in time branches serving customers across the UAE.

Rugby.title: Fight for Wales spots heats up as under-threat regions win
Rugby.summary: The talking points from round three of URC as Ospreys and Scarlets get first win and players try to impress Wales boss Steve Tandy.

There was western relief after Ospreys and Scarlets got up and running in the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship (URC) season. The two sides are playing amid uncertainty over their futures under controversial Welsh Rugby Union plans, yet produced the goods on the pitch in round three.

Ospreys won an engrossing derby against Dragons at Rodney Parade, inflicting a first defeat of the season on their hosts, while Scarlets sneaked past Benetton thanks to Sam Costelow's late penalty.

Rugby.title: Ulster playing games like training sessions
Rugby.summary: Head coach Richie Murphy says UIster are "playing matches like training sessions" as he expresses his disappointment after Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.
Rugby.copy:
Head coach Richie Murphy says Ulster are "playing matches like they're training sessions" as he expressed his disappointment with his side's slow start in Saturday's 26-26 draw with Munster in Belfast.

Trailing by 21 points at the break, Ulster hit back as Jacob Stockdale scored his second try of the game before David McCann and Stuart McCloskey struck to earn a second successive United Rugby Championship draw.

Rugby.title: Leinster stroll past Cardiff for happy homecoming

Champions Leinster made a successful return to the revamped Laya Arena by beating Cardiff in the United Rugby Championship (URC). The Irish province recorded their first victory of the 2026-27 season in front of 20,600 supporters, and condemned the Blue and Blacks to a first loss.

Leinster scored three tries inside the first quarter through Hugo Keenan, Jimmy O'Brien and Jack Conan, then O'Brien's second in the 37th minute secured the four-try bonus. But, with a raft of Ireland internationals making their first outings of the campaign, the second half was flat and scoreless until Jamie Osborne went over with five minutes to go.

Alexander Zverev is guaranteed to finish the 2026 season as world number one after Carlos Alcaraz's surprise defeat in the Shanghai Masters. German Zverev was on course to climb above current world number one Jannik Sinner, who has been ruled out for the rest of the year with a knee injury.

Alcaraz still had a mathematical chance of stopping Zverev until he was beaten 7-5 7-6 (7-4) by Belgium's Zizou Bergs in the third round on Monday. "It's been a fantastic season for me. Knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true," said Zverev.

Carlos Alcaraz’s campaign at the 2026 Shanghai Masters ended with a shock third round defeat, but how has the result impacted the ATP Rankings? The seven-time Grand Slam champion fell to a 7-5, 7-6(4) upset loss to 39th-ranked Zizou Bergs at the Masters 1000 tournament in Shanghai on Monday.

Alcaraz’s exit ended his six-match ATP Tour winning streak that included his second round victory in Shanghai and his successful title defence at the Japan Open earlier this month.

Tennis.title: Alexander Zverev’s first words as US Open champion clinches year-end No 1 after Carlos Alcaraz loss
Tennis.summary: What a year it has been Alexander Zverev! The post Alexander Zverev’s first words as US Open champion clinches year-end No 1 after Carlos Alcaraz loss appeared first on Tennis365 .
Tennis.copy:
Alexander Zverev says it is a “dream come true” that he will finish 2026 as the year-end No 1. With Jannik Sinner out for the rest of the season with a knee injury, Zverev was destined to finish the year as the world’s top-ranked player.

However, Carlos Alcaraz’s surprise third-round loss to Zizou Bergs at the Shanghai Open means nobody can catch the 29-year-old in the ATP Tour rankings. The German has enjoyed a magical year, winning both the French Open and US Open to finally break his Grand Slam duck. Now, the 6ft 6in player has opened up on a “fantastic” season that is getting better and better.

Tennis.title: Carlos Alcaraz vs Zizou Bergs controversy sparks calls for major tennis rule change after ‘unacceptable’ incident
Tennis.summary: "How is that allowed?" The post Carlos Alcaraz vs Zizou Bergs controversy sparks calls for major tennis rule change after ‘unacceptable’ incident appeared first on Tennis365 .
Tennis.copy:
Zizou Bergs secured an unforgettable victory over Carlos Alcaraz at the Shanghai Open but the Belgian has been criticised for his actions during the third-round match. Bergs upset second seed Alcaraz in just over two hours in a 7-5, 7-6 (4) victory at Qizhong Forest Sports City Arena on Monday for the biggest win of his career.

The 27-year-old was, naturally, emotional after this major scalp, particularly as he has struggled to get over the line in big matches. He said afterwards, “This is something that has been very tough for me. I often have too much respect for these guys, which is part of my culture and I’m proud of that. But it gets a little bit in the way when you have to play them. I had a great moment here last year against [Novak] Djokovic where I was definitely playing the name, not the guy.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu falls out of world’s top 100

Tennis.copy:
As on-court training resumes, she is understood to still be working with her coach Andrew Richardson, the old ally who guided her to the US Open trophy, and whose record with her remains outstanding after her strong performance at Queen’s in June.

In the short term, Australia is sure to be Raducanu’s primary target. Her record at Melbourne’s Australian Open is indifferent, with four of her five appearances having ended in the second round. In 2025, she went one better, scratching out nuggety wins over Ekaterina Alexandrova and Amanda Anisimova – two quality players – before being annihilated by Iga Swiatek in the third round.

Tennis.title: Highlights as Carlos Alcaraz was dumped out in the third round of the Shanghai Masters by Zizou Bergs
Tennis.summary: Highlights as Carlos Alcaraz was dumped out in the third round of the Shanghai Masters by Zizou Bergs Sky Sports
Tennis.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz was dumped out in the third round of the Shanghai Masters as Zizou Bergs recorded the biggest win of his career, with the Spaniard's defeat confirming Alexander Zverev as the year-end world No 1.

Bergs beat the second seed 7-5 7-6 (7-4), recovering to win the second set in a tie-break after failing to serve out the match at 6-5. Alcaraz's exit, coupled with current world No 1 Jannik Sinner ending his campaign early due to a knee problem that has sidelined him since Wimbledon, means Zverev will end 2026 top of the rankings for the first time.

Tennis.title: What Carlos Alcaraz was heard yelling at his coach during Shanghai Masters loss to Zizou Bergs

Tennis.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz struggled in his third-round match against Zizou Bergs in the third round of the Shanghai Masters. The Spaniard arrived at the penultimate Masters tournament of the calendar in good form, having lifted the Japan Open title for the second year in a row.

He began his campaign with a solid straight-sets victory against Juan Manuel Cerundolo in his opening round match in Shanghai, but he did not play his best tennis as he lost in straight sets to Bergs.

Tennis.title: Zizou Berg’s immediate reaction after stunning win over Carlos Alcaraz in Shanghai
Tennis.summary: Zizou Bergs stunned after stunning win over Carlos Alcaraz. The post Zizou Berg’s immediate reaction after stunning win over Carlos Alcaraz in Shanghai appeared first on Tennis365 .
Tennis.copy:
Zizou Bergs was not quite sure “what was going on” after his stunning win over Carlos Alcaraz at the Shanghai Masters, admitting he was in “disbelief”. The world No 39 claimed the biggest win of his career as he beat seven-time Grand Slam winner Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6 (7-5) in just over two hours in the third round of the ATP Masters 1000 event.

It is only his third top-10 win following victories over world No 9 Andrey Rublev at the 2025 Miami Open and world No 5 Felix Auger-Aliassime at this year’s United Cup. Alcaraz was the overwhelming favourite as he is fresh from winning the Japan Open and also cruised past Juan Manuel Cerundolo in the second round, but never got his nose in front as the Belgian broke in game five before the second seed got back on terms in the next game.

Tennis.title: Carlos Alcaraz prize money and ranking points from shock Shanghai Open exit
Tennis.summary: Nobody saw this coming! The post Carlos Alcaraz prize money and ranking points from shock Shanghai Open exit appeared first on Tennis365 .
Tennis.copy:
Zizou Bergs pulled off the biggest win of his career after knocking out Carlos Alcaraz from the Shanghai Open on Monday. The Belgian held his nerve in a 7-5, 7-6 (4) victory in two hours and two minutes to set up a fourth-round clash with either defending champion Valentin Vacherot or Tommy Paul.

Alcaraz was out of sorts against the world No 43, as he perhaps felt the effects of his title run in Tokyo, with the seven-time major champion hitting seven winners and 17 unforced errors in the first set.

Tennis.title: WTA Rankings: Mirra Andreeva passes Jessica Pegula & Coco Gauff; Zheng Qinwen +31, Emma Raducanu at No 107
Tennis.summary: This way for your post-China Open WTA Rankings. The post WTA Rankings: Mirra Andreeva passes Jessica Pegula & Coco Gauff; Zheng Qinwen +31, Emma Raducanu at No 107 appeared first on Tennis365 .

Elena Rybakina maintains a healthy lead in the rankings ahead of Aryna Sabalenka while Mirra Andreeva has cracked a new career-high and Zheng Qinwen surged 31 places. Three-time Grand Slam winner Rybakina started her fourth week at No 1 in the WTA Rankings on Monday and her second-round exit from the China Open didn’t cost her too much as her main rival Aryna Sabalenka also didn’t fare well.

Rybakina lost her first match since becoming world No 1 as she was stunned by Alina Charaeva in Beijing, but with Sabalenka losing in the next round against Nikola Bartunkova, the gap between the two is 2,146 points.

Tennis.title: Wuhan Open withdrawal list: 15 WTA stars out as Zheng Qinwen and two Grand Slam winners also pull out

The 2026 Wuhan Open has been dealt another couple of blows as Chinese hero Zheng Qinwen has joined the list of big-name players to pull out of the WTA 1000 event. “I’m very sorry to share that I will be withdrawing from this year’s Wuhan Open,” she said in a statement. “Wuhan is where my tennis dream began, and the Wuhan Open is also where I made my breakthrough at the WTA 1000 level. I have always looked forward to competing in front of my hometown fans.

Tennis.title: Fit-again Kartal beats top-50 opponent in Wuhan
Tennis.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal continues her impressive form since returning from injury by beating Anhelina Kalinina in straight sets to reach the second round of the Wuhan Open.
Tennis.copy:
Sonay Kartal says she has "thrown herself in the deep end" since returning from a six-month injury absence after beating Anhelina Kalinina to reach the Wuhan Open second round.

The British number five, 24, reached the third round at the Beijing Open earlier this month in her first WTA tournament since suffering a stress fracture in her back. She followed that up by defeating Ukraine's Kalinina 7-5 6-3 in an hour and 31 minutes in Wuhan.

Tennis.title: China Open: Qinwen Zheng stuns Mirra Andreeva to make history as first Chinese winner of WTA event in Beijing
Tennis.summary: China Open: Qinwen Zheng stuns Mirra Andreeva to make history as first Chinese winner of WTA event in Beijing Sky Sports
Tennis.copy:
Olympic champion Qinwen Zheng made history as the first Chinese player to win the China Open on Sunday, stunning French Open winner Mirra Andreeva 7-5 6-4. Wild card Zheng, who has been on a recovery path after missing nearly six months due to an elbow injury on her dominant right arm, looked like her old self as she used powerful forehands to control the rallies, and landed swift winners angling away from Andreeva.

After the two exchanged early breaks, world No 5 Andreeva held firm to go 5-4 up, and almost got a decisive break when Zheng sent a cross-court shot too long before netting a forehand.

Tennis.title: Karaoke-singing Zheng makes history with China Open win
Tennis.summary: Zheng Qinwen becomes the first Chinese champion of the China Open after overcoming Mirra Andreeva in straight sets.
Tennis.copy:
Zheng Qinwen became the first Chinese woman to win the China Open by beating Mirra Andreeva in Beijing. Zheng, who entered the tournament as a wildcard ranked number 54 in the world, saved three set points in Sunday's opener before overcoming fourth seed Andreeva 7-5 6-4.

The 24-year-old fell to the floor after converting match point and treated the raucous home crowd to some karaoke following her victory speech. "The feeling was incredible. To win here in Beijing in front of my home crowd is one of my dreams," she said.

Tennis.title: Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard displays new look in victory at Shanghai Masters as Mirra Andreeva, Qinwen Zheng make China Open final
Tennis.summary: Carlos Alcaraz: Spaniard displays new look in victory at Shanghai Masters as Mirra Andreeva, Qinwen Zheng make China Open final Sky Sports

Carlos Alcaraz's exceptional touch at the net, alongside a slick new look, was on full display during his opening victory at the Shanghai Masters on Saturday. The world No 3, sporting a freshly trimmed moustache, delivered an aggressive performance to defeat Juan Manuel Cerundolo 6-3 6-3 and reach the third round of the ATP Masters 1000 event.

Alcaraz repeatedly surged forward with purpose during their 66-minute encounter, showcasing his deft touch to extend his winning streak to seven matches following his successful title defence in Tokyo.

Golf.copy:
Whatever becomes of LIV Golf 2.0, the DP World Tour has decided it won’t let those who compete in the rebel circuit’s new version have it both ways. In a statement to BBC Sport, DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings said the European circuit, which had previously reached agreements with LIV players to allow them into its tournaments, will no longer do so in 2027, effectively banning them from playing.

“Players need to make a choice,” Kinnings told BBC Sport. “We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by. Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour.”

Former European Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley says the DP World Tour has "a right to compete for business" after the circuit confirmed players intending to compete on LIV Golf in 2027 will not be eligible for membership.

Sunday saw a host of young and journeyman pros alike experience the highlight of their careers: earning PGA Tour cards at the 2026 Korn Ferry Tour Championship. As happens every year, heartwarming tales about players’ big achievements abound. But there is another side to the story: the other pros who just missed out on their Tour cards.

But instead of fleeing the course as fast as he could, a “dejected” Hammer faced the cameras and opened up about his unfortunate fate. In the process, he showed a hard-earned perspective that should serve him well as he continues his pro career.

Jon Rahm has announced his first start since declaring he has quit LIV Golf. Last week, it was revealed in LIV’s bankruptcy courts that Rahm would not be signing up to the post-Saudi version of the breakaway league.

Players who sign up to play on a resurrected LIV Golf tour will be prohibited from competing on the DP World Tour or in the Ryder Cup, its European chiefs have said. The rebel golf league has secured funding from BC Partners to exit bankruptcy proceedings after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund pulled its backing earlier this year.

Players including Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm and Cameron Smith have been offered equity in the new business and given until 25 October to pledge their continued allegiance. Rahm’s lawyer said he will not partake in the new season.

Golf.title: Meet the 20 pros who just earned 2027 PGA Tour cards
Golf.summary: Twenty pros grabbed 2027 PGA Tour cards via their finish during the 2026 Korn Ferry Tour season. Here's who earned a promotion. The post Meet the 20 pros who just earned 2027 PGA Tour cards appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
If you haven’t heard, big changes are coming to the PGA Tour in 2028. With the Tour’s two-track system debuting in a little over a year, that means next season, 2027, will be critical for players trying to play their way onto the top tier, the Championship Series.

And you know what’s really going to help accomplish that? By already owning a PGA Tour card in 2027. Twenty players just did that — including a 19-year-old pro — as they earned a promotion via the season-ending Korn Ferry Tour Championship Sunday. Now those guys have a head start in getting on the top track come 2028.

Golf.title: Teenage phenom earns Tour card, sets record the hard way
Golf.summary: You've likely heard his name before, but you're about to see a lot more of this 19-year-old on the PGA Tour next season. The post Teenage phenom earns Tour card, sets record the hard way appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Sunday may not have been the exact result 19-year-old Blades Brown was looking for — a fourth 54-hole lead squandered — but it ultimately saw him earn what he wanted next: a season full of starts on the PGA Tour.

Brown is well known to this point, partly due to his golfy name and partly due to his impressive game. He turned pro at just 17 and has played on the Korn Ferry Tour much of the last two seasons, occasionally sprinkling in some starts on the PGA Tour. He flashed in moments this summer, never quite getting across the line for a win, but the floor has been extremely high. He’s made 16 of 18 cuts and finished in the top 10 five times.

Golf.title: Forrest earns major invites with Spanish Open win
Golf.summary: Scotland's Grant Forrest holds off a charge from home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open and book a spot at The Open and the Masters next year.
Golf.copy:
Scotland's Grant Forrest held off a charge from home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open and book a spot at The Open and the Masters next year. With Chacarra in the clubhouse at 13 under, Forrest and playing partner Victor Perez needed to make birdies at the 18th to go above the Spaniard.

Both players' drives nestled down in the greenside rough on the 322-yard par four, and after Perez's birdie putt drifted past the hole, Forrest sunk his to seal his third DP World Tour title and a first professional win outside Scotland.

Golf.title: How Bernhard Langer unintentionally taught future pro important lesson
Golf.summary: Alistair Docherty joined GOLF's Subpar podcast to discuss finally earning his PGA Tour card, his first golf memory and more. The post How Bernhard Langer unintentionally taught future pro important lesson appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Alistair Docherty’s first golf memory provided a couple of valuable lessons. The 32-year-old pro, who will be a PGA Tour card-holder for the first time come 2027, joined this week’s GOLF Subpar podcast and explained how a trip to Sahalee Country Club played a key role in his life.

Sahalee is a private country club in Sammamish, Wash., just outside of Seattle, and in 2010 it hosted the U.S. Senior Open. (It was also home to the 1998 PGA Championship, won by Vijay Singh.) But in 2010, Docherty attended the U.S. Senior Open with his father, and they found a spot to sit by the 10th tee.

Golf.title: 'Fairytale stuff': Pro's hard year ends with ticket to 2027 Masters
Golf.summary: Grant Forrest has had a year to forget. But that all changed on Sunday in Spain, where he punched an unlikely ticket to the 2027 Masters. The post ‘Fairytale stuff’: Pro’s hard year ends with ticket to 2027 Masters appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Eleven years ago, Grant Forrest had a ticket to the Masters in his grasp. Then a budding Scottish amateur star, Forrest reached the finals of the 2015 Amateur Championship. A win meant not only one of amateur golf’s biggest prizes but also a trip to Magnolia Lane. But a 4&2 loss to Romain Langasque meant Forrest’s Augusta National dream would have to wait.

The wait wasn’t expected to be long. Forrest made the 2015 Walker Cup team and was expected to be one of Europe’s bright young stars. But golf had other plans. Forrest turned pro and worked his way up from the Challenge Tour to the DP World Tour, finally reaching the top European circuit in 2019. His first DP World Tour win arrived at the 2021 Hero Open. His next came four years later at the 2025 Nexo Championship. Along the way, Forrest played in two Open Championships and one U.S. Open, but never played well enough to reach Augusta National.

Golf.copy:
Michael Brennan clearly plays his best golf at the end of the year as he just picked up his third PGA Tour victory and his second in the month of October. After winning the Wyndham Championship in August, Brennan took home the Baycurrent Classic on Sunday in Japan.

At Yokohama Country Club, Brennan used the same all-Titleist setup he used for his Wyndham win in August, including the Scotty Cameron Golo 6 Tour Prototype he switched to earlier this season.

Golf.copy:
Sunday at Yokohama Country Club began with a packed leaderboard and a world of possibilities. It ended with Michael Brennan holding off Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell to win the Baycurrent Classic, his third PGA Tour title in 12 months.

“Unbelievable. It was an unbelievable week. Japan was spectacular, the fans were amazing this week,” Brennan said after his win. Mitchell, who is still searching for his first win since the 2019 Honda Classic, took the lead on the front nine with three birdies and an eagle. But he dropped shots at Nos. 9 and 12, leaving him one shot behind Brennan coming down the stretch. Mitchell striped his tee shot on 18 and left himself a 10-foot birdie putt to tie Brennan at 16 under, but he couldn’t get it to fall.

THFC.title: Man City's Omar Marmoush fined over uninsured McLaren
THFC.summary: The DVLA tried to contact the footballer at his former Manchester address, court papers show.
THFC.copy:
Tottenham striker Omar Marmoush has been fined after his McLaren supercar was found to be uninsured and not declared off the road. The 27-year-old, who joined Spurs on loan from Manchester City in August, was found guilty at Teesside Magistrates' Court on 5 October.

He was fined £220 and ordered to pay £100 in costs and an £88 victim surcharge, according to the Press Association (PA). The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) brought the prosecution after Marmoush failed to pay a fixed penalty issued in June.

THFC.title: Rodrigo Bentancur agreement reached as Tottenham sent clear verdict on Man Utd red card
THFC.summary: Rodrigo Bentancur agreement reached as Tottenham sent clear verdict on Man Utd red card Football London
THFC.copy:
Tottenham Hotspur have been given a clear verdict on Rodrigo Bentancur's red card against Manchester United after the Uruguay international was sent off for violent conduct. The 29-year-old was sent off in the 78th minute, with United leading 1-0 thanks to a goal from Bryan Mbeumo. The Spurs man went flying into a tackle with Luke Shaw, before the defender reacted by pushing Bentancur.

The Spurs star appeared to headbutt the United full-back leaving the referee with little choice but to send him off. Fortunately for Roberto De Zerbi, Dominic Solanke popped up with a late equaliser to ensure a share of the spoils.

THFC.title: Lewis family increase Tottenham stake after £320m injection as Daniel Levy share shrinks
THFC.summary: Lewis family increase Tottenham stake after £320m injection as Daniel Levy share shrinks Football London
THFC.copy:
The Lewis family have increased their stake in Tottenham after their recent £120million cash boost while former chairman Daniel Levy's slice of the club has shrunk. The family, who own Spurs through investment company ENIC, have backed the Premier League club's attempts to transform to a more successful outfit with £320million injected into it over the past 12 months. Vivienne Lewis and her son-in-law Nick Beucher have taken a more active role in backing CEO Vinai Venkatesham and non-executive chairman Peter Charrington and the family have resisted interest from various parties in selling the club in the past couple of years.

The latest £120million injection for working capital has now officially increased the family's stake in Spurs to 89.06 per cent and after former chairman Levy did not take up the opportunity to match the cash boost with his own relative part of it, his slice in ENIC's pie at Tottenham has dwindled from being 29.8 per cent in October last year to 27.38 in June this year and now 25 per cent after two missed injection opportunities.

THFC.title: What Tottenham games Rodrigo Bentancur will miss as Premier League red card rules explained
THFC.summary: What Tottenham games Rodrigo Bentancur will miss as Premier League red card rules explained Football London

Rodrigo Bentancur will miss some huge Premier League games for Tottenham Hotspur due to suspension. Roberto De Zerbi will be without Rodrigo Bentancur for three Premier League games, having been sent off for violent conduct during Tottenham Hotspur's hard-fought draw with Manchester United.

In the final quarter of an hour at Old Trafford on Saturday night, the ball broke free down the left-hand side, and, desperate to extinguish the assault on his backline, the Lilywhites midfielder dived into a tackle on Luke Shaw. The Red Devils defender hurdled Bentancur, who won the ball.

THFC.title: The 'Kane-esque' striker Spurs may regret letting go
THFC.summary: Will Lankshear's positioning, finishing and poacher's instinct have made him an instant hit at Riverside Stadium – and a cause of lament at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
THFC.copy:
Leaping high, six yards out, to nod in Tommy Conway's cross from the left wing, Will Lankshear notched his ninth goal in 12 games for Middlesbrough. It is that positioning, finishing and poacher's instinct, earning Boro a 1-0 win against Wolves on Saturday, that has made Lankshear an instant hit at Riverside Stadium – and a cause of lament at Tottenham Hotspur.

Lankshear joined Boro from Spurs in the summer on a five-year contract in a deal that could rise to a club record buy of £20m. Since then, he has scored as many goals in all competitions as Spurs' combined team. His old side, despite snatching a draw at Manchester United a few hours after Lankshear's latest winner, remain in the Premier League relegation zone while Boro sit in the Championship's automatic promotion places.

THFC.title: Tottenham Hotspur Stadium breaks new record amid dramatic moment
THFC.summary: Tottenham Hotspur Stadium breaks new record amid dramatic moment Football London
THFC.copy:
The Tottenham Hotspur Stadium broke their NFL crowd record during a dramatic encounter as the Jacksonville Jaguars secured a last-gasp win against the Philadelphia Eagles. Spurs had enjoyed their own dramatic moment in Manchester on Saturday as Dominic Solanke headed home a 92nd minute equaliser at Old Trafford and the following day their stadium in north London provided the backdrop to a fascinating encounter with a eye-catching start and conclusion in the second of the NFL London Games held in N17 this year.

From the opening kick-off, Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. got into a fight in the middle of the field with the Jaguars' defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. with staff and players from both sides pouring on to stop it. Both players were ejected within seconds of the contest.

THFC.title: Tottenham's fastest player in Manchester United draw might surprise you
THFC.summary: Tottenham's fastest player in Manchester United draw might surprise you Football London
THFC.copy:
Tottenham took home a point from their dramatic 1-1 draw at Manchester United on Saturday and one of their summer signings logged the fastest sprint among the starters on the day.

Spurs dominated much of the first half in Manchester, frustrating the home fans with Conor Gallagher and Dominic Solanke thwarted by the keeper late in the first half before Solanke fired over inside the six-yard box early in the second period.

THFC.title: Alan Shearer lays into Tottenham star after Man Utd draw - 'Nowhere near good enough'
THFC.summary: Alan Shearer lays into Tottenham star after Man Utd draw - 'Nowhere near good enough' Football London
THFC.copy:
Alan Shearer has slammed Tottenham star Dominic Solanke's time at Spurs as 'nowhere near good enough' and said the forward is lacking confidence. The Premier League record goalscorer was not impressed with Solanke's impact against Manchester United.

The Lilywhites striker scored his first Premier League goal of the season against the Red Devils with a smart header after holding off Lisandro Martinez. But it was his wayward efforts throughout the match that frustrated Shearer.

THFC.title: De Zerbi has his Pochettino moment and the strange decision during Tottenham's draw at Man United
THFC.summary: De Zerbi has his Pochettino moment and the strange decision during Tottenham's draw at Man United Football London
THFC.copy:
It started with a kiss. Well technically it started with a push and then a coming together of heads. Whatever it started with, the script finally ended differently for Tottenham Hotspur. The familiar tale this season of playing well, failing to take chances and coming away with nothing did not come to pass.

It had looked like it was heading that way, Spurs dominant in the first half with the ball and creating big chances for Dominic Solanke at the start of both periods and Conor Gallagher before the interval.

THFC.title: 'I kissed Rodrigo and said thanks'
THFC.summary: Roberto de Zerbi praises Rodrigo Bentancur after he was sent off in a 1-1 draw against Manchester United.
THFC.copy:
Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi praised Rodrigo Bentancur after he was sent off in the 1-1 draw against Manchester United. The Uruguay midfielder was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw during a feisty 78th-minute melee when Spurs were trailing 1-0 at Old Trafford.

Despite being reduced to 10 men, Tottenham managed to salvage a point as Dominic Solanke headed home in the second minute of added time. Spurs remain winless in the Premier League this season after six games, but De Zerbi was thankful to Bentancur for providing a "spark" against United.

THFC.title: Roberto De Zerbi explains why he left out Micky Van de Ven for Man Utd clash as youngster trusted
THFC.summary: Roberto De Zerbi explains why he left out Micky Van de Ven for Man Utd clash as youngster trusted Football London
THFC.copy:
Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi revealed that he was managing Micky van de Ven's minutes after leaving the defender out of his starting lineup against Manchester United. Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi were Roberto De Zerbi's central defensive pairing of choice as Archie Gray and Destiny Udogie completed the back four. Van de Ven eventually came onto the pitch after Mbeumo's goal, replacing Udogie.

The Dutchman started all four Netherlands matches during the international break, against Germany, Serbia away, Greece and Serbia at home, and went off injured. He did, however, fail to keep a clean sheet as former Barcelona star Xavi took charge of the team for the first time.

THFC.title: Solanke saves wasteful Spurs
THFC.summary: Dominic Solanke scores in stoppage time to salvage a draw for a wasteful 10-man Tottenham.
THFC.copy:
Like so many of their matches so far this season, Tottenham were the better team to start with and they penned Manchester United in with their high press and quick tempo. But once again they lacked conviction in front of goal and were left to rue missed early chances, with Dominic Solanke, Mohammed Kudus and Conor Gallagher all failing to find the back of the net in the opening 45 minutes.

For the 18th time in 2026, Spurs were unable to score in the first half of a Premier League game and they could not assert the same level of control after the break as United responded.
